title: Misdiagnosis and mistreatment of a common side-effect--angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor-induced cough
authors: Vegter S, de Jong-van den Berg LT
followUp: dispensing data 2000 to 2007; half-year window around ACE inhibitor initiation
population: Incident users of ACE inhibitors in the Dutch IADB.nl pharmacy dispensing database
funder: not read: the available full-text record contains only the abstract, which carries no funding statement.
result: Prescription sequence symmetry analysis: of 1054 patients starting both an ACE inhibitor and an antitussive within half a year, 703 received the antitussive after and 351 before the ACE inhibitor, adjusted sequence ratio 2.2 (95% CI 1.9 to 2.4); women were more likely to receive antitussives after initiation (odds ratio 1.4, 1.1 to 1.9). The authors estimate that 15% of ACE-inhibitor cough is treated with antitussives instead of substitution.
